subject: Math
subskill: Effect of Adding/Removing Data on Statistics
prompt:
[Figure 1]

The histogram summarizes a data set of the weights, in pounds, of $14$ tuna. If an additional weight of $120$ pounds is added to the original data set to create a new data set of $15$ weights of tuna, which of the following measures must be greater for the new data set than for the original data set?

I. The median
II. The mean
explanation: Choice B is correct. The original data set contains $14$ tuna with weights distributed across five intervals. Since there are $14$ values (an even number), the median is the average of the $7$th and $8$th values when ordered. Based on the histogram: $2$ tuna have weights in the $15$-$25$ pound range (positions $1$-$2$) and $6$ tuna have weights in the $25$-$35$ pound range (positions $3$-$8$). Therefore, both the $7$th and $8$th values are in the $25$-$35$ pound range, so the median lies in this interval. When a weight of $120$ pounds is added to create a new data set of $15$ tuna, the median becomes the $8$th value. Since $120$ pounds is the largest value, it is placed last when ordered, leaving the positions of the first $14$ values unchanged, so the $8$th value is still in the $25$-$35$ pound range. Therefore, the median does not necessarily increase. The mean equals the sum of all values divided by the number of values. The original mean must be less than $65$, so adding a value of $120$ pounds, which is far greater than the original mean, must pull the new mean upward. Therefore, only the mean must be greater for the new data set.
